fixes.title: Registration reports a 10.34px alignment residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field, so even the working path cannot stack; match_radius_px defaults to 50px
fixes.summary: Wave 6 had closed this by adding fit_transform_robust (median-based sigma clipping) and tightening max_alignment_residual_px 10.0 -> 2.0. I re-tested it adversarially and the clipping is INERT against the exact failure the finding describes. Reproduced: 20 honest pairs on a rigid (-1, +2) translation plus 8 pairs stolen from the neighbour 45px away, all displaced the SAME direction -> fit_transform_robust returned residual 18.461px, inliers 28 (nothing clipped at all), transform (-3.03, -8.08) instead of (-1, +2). Median clipping only works when the wrong pairs scatter: a coherent bloc drags the fit bodily towards itself until the honest pairs sit as far from it as the stolen ones, the 3x-median cutoff then covers the whole set, and the loop exits on pass 1 having removed nothing. Algebraically it goes inert once the coherent bloc passes ~25% of the pairs. A steal chain is coherent by construction, so wave 6 fixed the scattered case and left the reported one. Fixed in two places. (1) stacking.rs match_stars is now MUTUAL nearest neighbour instead of a greedy brightest-first search that CONSUMED the frame star it picked: a pair is kept only when each star is the other's closest admissible candidate. That stops the chain at its seed -- an orphaned bright reference star can no longer take a frame star sitting 2px from its real owner and 47px from itself, so the displacement never propagates along the field. (2) stacking.rs fit_transform_robust now runs a consensus (RANSAC-style) stage before the clipping loop: it seeds a rigid transform from every admissible pair of matches and keeps the largest set agreeing within 2px, which is indifferent to how the errors are distributed because a coherently-wrong bloc simply describes a different transform and loses the vote. Guarded three ways so it cannot invert into new rejections -- it only runs when the plain fit is already inconsistent (>1.0px), and is adopted only when the agreeing set keeps >= min_matched_pairs, holds >= 60% of the matches, AND lowers the residual. The 60% dominance floor is load-bearing for safety, not decoration: a genuinely non-rigid frame splits its stars into two real blocs, and aligning to the larger one would resample the smaller one pixels away and fold that smear into the stack permanently. Without that floor the pre-existing add_frame_rejects_high_alignment_residual test (a frame where half the stars shift (3,2) and half (9,8)) started PASSING -- consensus rescued a frame that must stay rejected. Deliberately did NOT touch match_radius_px (50.0) or match_flux_tolerance (0.7): shrinking the radius would just relocate the defect onto legitimate dithers and large mount shifts, which is the trap the finding's own proposed_fix walks into.
fixes.test: 3 new tests in native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs: match_stars_refuses_to_let_an_orphan_steal_a_claimed_star, a_coherent_steal_chain_is_broken_by_consensus_not_clipping, add_frame_registers_a_dense_field_a_consuming_matcher_would_chain. The end-to-end one drives the real add_frame path on a 64-star field (columns 45px apart, inside the match radius; rows 60px apart, outside it, so mis-pairing can only run along a row) with the leading star of 4 rows missing from the frame. Under a consuming matcher that leaves under 60% of pairs honest -- deliberately past the point where consensus is allowed to help, so only the matcher fix can carry it.
fixes.revert_check: REVERT A: restored the greedy consuming body of match_stars (the `used_frame_indices` loop, stacking.rs:733-790) -- match_stars_refuses_to_let_an_orphan_steal_a_claimed_star FAILED, and add_frame_registers_a_dense_field_a_consuming_matcher_would_chain FAILED with `Alignment residual too high: 15.75px (max 2.00px)`, i.e. the reported symptom exactly: a rigid 2px shift refused for a double-digit residual. REVERT B: deleted the `if residual > CONSENSUS_TRIGGER_PX { ... }` block from fit_transform_robust (stacking.rs:1030-1045) -- a_coherent_steal_chain_is_broken_by_consensus_not_clipping FAILED. Restored both: 30/30 stacking tests pass, full package 503 + 12 + 1 pass, cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets clean.
fixes.caveats: The original audit_L_018.fits / audit_L_024.fits are gone from the machine, so revalidation against those exact frames is still owed (wave 6 owed the same). The finding's caveat (c) -- that detect_stars returns 0 stars on audit_L_001.fits where an independent peak finder reads 40 -- is a separate detector-sensitivity defect and is still NOT addressed; it produces an 'Insufficient stars' rejection, not a residual, so it is a different observable. Consensus is O(n^2) hypotheses x O(n) scoring, bounded by MAX_CONSENSUS_HYPOTHESES = 8000 and by max_match_stars = 100 (4950 hypotheses worst case), and only runs on frames that already fail the plain fit.

fixes.title: The Alpaca server address can never be set: 'Query Alpaca on startup' points at a 'configured Alpaca server' that no screen in the app configures
fixes.summary: Closed by a later wave, and closed at both ends. The editor now exists: connection_settings.dart:195-217 renders an 'Alpaca Server Address' SettingRow whose subtitle is the live '${settings.alpacaServerHost}:${settings.alpacaServerPort}' and whose Configure button opens AlpacaServerDialog (connection_settings.dart:13 imports it); connection_settings_alpaca_dialog.dart mirrors IndiServerDialog with host/port fields, per-field validation that refuses a malformed port instead of coercing it (:81-105), a Test Connection that calls discoverAlpacaAtAddress and treats an EMPTY device list as failure rather than success (:126-135), and a Save that calls setAlpacaServerHost/setAlpacaServerPort (:161-162). The row is deliberately NOT platform-gated the way the INDI row above it is (:167 `if (!Platform.isWindows)`), which is correct -- _getAvailableBackends lists Alpaca on every platform (unified_discovery_provider.dart:320-321). I verified the finding's 'grep returns nothing' claim is now false and, more importantly, traced the OTHER end, which the finding's real damage claim rests on ('the Alpaca discovery address is therefore permanently localhost:11111'): unified_discovery_provider.dart:394-396 reads `host ?? settings.alpacaServerHost` / `port ?? settings.alpacaServerPort` and passes them to discoverAlpacaAtAddress, and the startup path reaches exactly that code -- auto_discovery_launcher.dart:109 passes `includeAlpaca: settings.alpacaAutoDiscover` into discoverAll (:132), which calls _discoverBackend(DriverType.alpaca) with no host/port so the settings fallback applies. That consumption side is unchanged from HEAD (git diff shows no modification to unified_discovery_provider.dart), i.e. it was always correct and only the editor was missing. The one other discoverAlpacaAtAddress caller, headless_api/handlers/device_discovery_handlers.dart:224-239, is an explicit-address endpoint that requires host+port query params, so it has no stored-address path to get wrong. WHAT I ADDED: the wave's tests covered only the UI half, so a regression that made discovery ignore the stored address would have gone unnoticed -- a stored address nothing reads is the same defect wearing a UI. Added a consumption-side test.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/alpaca_discovery_address_test.dart (new, 3 tests) drives the real unifiedDiscoveryProvider.discoverAll() and verifies the backend was asked for the stored address: 'startup discovery queries the configured Alpaca host and port', 'the stored Alpaca address is not confused with the INDI one', 'Alpaca is not queried at all when the startup toggle is off'. Plus the pre-existing packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_alpaca_address_test.dart (2 tests) for the editor.
fixes.revert_check: CONSUMPTION SIDE: replaced unified_discovery_provider.dart:395-396 with `final alpacaHost = host ?? 'localhost'; final alpacaPort = port ?? 11111;` -- exactly the behaviour the finding describes. 2 of the 3 new tests failed (the third, the toggle-off one, correctly still passed since it asserts no call at all). Restored: 3/3 pass. UI SIDE: deleted the whole 'Alpaca Server Address' SettingRow from connection_settings.dart -- both tests in connection_alpaca_address_test.dart failed. Restored: 2/2 pass.
fixes.caveats: Not driven live against a real ASCOM Remote host; the Test Connection button's behaviour against an actually-reachable Alpaca server is unverified here.

fixes.title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query -- the error survives Retry and a tab round-trip, and only a full app restart clears it
fixes.summary: Split verdict, because the finding was two claims and they resolve differently. CLAIM 1 (the dead Retry) was already closed by wave 6, deeper than its own report suggested: transient_detections_dao.dart:96-112 adds _mapSkippingUndecodable and BOTH read paths use it (:79 watchRecentDetections, :128 recentDetections), so one undecodable row costs that row and never the feed -- the only demonstrated route into the error state is gone. CLAIM 2 (the feed is a one-shot read taken at app launch) is NOT REAL, which is what the verifier asked to be re-tested with an in-app write: I wrote that test ('a detection persisted after the feed is live shows up') and it passes on the shipped code. BUT re-testing it turned up a real, narrower defect inside the same promise, which wave 6 knew about and deliberately left: its `.skip(1)` discards the change stream's first event, and that event is the ONLY delivery a detection gets if it is persisted after the feed's opening read returns but before the feed has subscribed -- nothing is listening yet, so the write's notification reaches no one. I reproduced it: a candidate written in that window never appeared, polled for 2 full seconds, and it would stay missing until some LATER detection happened to refresh the feed. During a run that is a transient the operator is never shown, silently, while the panel promises 'Anything that appeared, moved, or brightened on a deep patch lands here to review'. FIXED by restructuring the feed (transient_detections_provider.dart _liveDetectionsFeed): subscribe to the DB watch FIRST so the window closes, and use that watch purely as a change SIGNAL, serving every emission from a fresh one-shot read. That also removes the reason `.skip(1)` existed -- a re-read can never be staler than the replay it would have discarded -- and routes the watch stream's own errors into another fresh read instead of forwarding them, which structurally kills the original 'Retry replays a cached failure' defect independently of the DAO decode being defensive. Reads are sequence-guarded so a slower older read cannot overwrite a newer one. SECOND CALL SITE: the finding named only First Light, but science_export_hub.dart:509 renders the same Retry (`ref.invalidate(allTransientDetectionsProvider)`) over the sibling feed, and transient_alert_provider.dart:553 listens to it to update the alert bell -- same two hazards, same provider shape. allTransientDetectionsProvider now shares _liveDetectionsFeed too. The per-session transientDetectionsProvider family was left alone: it has zero production consumers (grep for 'transientDetectionsProvider(' outside tests returns nothing) and is behind no Retry.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/first_light_live_feed_test.dart (new, 5 tests): 'a detection persisted after the feed is live shows up' (this is the one that DISPROVES the finding's second claim), 'a detection persisted while the feed is opening is not lost', 'a replayed cached failure does not resurrect the error state', plus the same two guarantees asserted against allTransientDetectionsProvider for the export hub / alert bell. The race is driven by a DAO subclass that performs the insert inside recentDetections, which lands the write in exactly the blind window rather than hoping to hit it by timing.
fixes.revert_check: FEED SHAPE: restored `yield await dao.recentDetections(...); yield* dao.watchRecentDetections(...).skip(1);` -- 'a detection persisted while the feed is opening is not lost' FAILED and 'a replayed cached failure does not resurrect the error state' FAILED; 'a detection persisted after the feed is live shows up' still passed, which is correct since that behaviour was never broken. SECOND CALL SITE: reverted allTransientDetectionsProvider to `dao.watchRecentDetections(limit: kFirstLightFeedLimit)` -- both export-hub tests FAILED while the First Light ones stayed green, proving the second call site is independently wired. Restored: 5/5 pass, plus wave 6's 4 resilience tests. Full skotiq_core suite 5461 passed / 4 skipped / 6 failed, where the 6 are pre-existing NINA-import failures verified identical with the provider checked out at HEAD (+14 -6 both ways). skotiq_app test/screens/first_light/ + test/screens/settings/connection_alpaca_address_test.dart: 17/17 pass. skotiq_app test/screens/analytics/ has one failure, captures_landscape_test.dart 'analytics phone landscape 932x430', also verified pre-existing with the provider at HEAD. dart analyze clean on the changed file.
fixes.caveats: Marked 'partial' rather than 'fixed' because the finding's headline (the dead Retry) was already closed before this wave and I am claiming credit only for the residual; and 'not-real' does not fit either, since the second claim being false is what exposed the race that WAS real. Not re-driven through the live GUI -- the original repro needed an externally-corrupted DB row, and that route no longer produces an error state at all. Each change notification now costs one extra bounded query (LIMIT 200 over an index range); detections are rare events so this is not a hot path.
